  "text": "Anne put her hand over her mouth.

The boy looked for his schoolbag, though he knew it was upstairs, hanging from the bedpost. His mother pulled gently on the thread. Something tightened beneath his ribs.

“Stop,” he said.

She let it slacken at once.

Neither father moved. That frightened him more than the bowl.

“I only opened the seam,” Anne said. “There wasn't room for everything.”

“For what?” his mother asked.

Anne looked at the boy.

He remembered packing for his grandmother's. Socks, the green jumper, the book with the missing last page. But that was tomorrow. He remembered his father telling him to hurry. He remembered being halfway down the stairs when the telephone rang.

The other father closed his eyes.

“No,” his mother said, watching the boy's face. “He doesn't need that one.”

From the kitchen came the small, dry sound of an orange rolling across the table. It fell without striking the floor.

His father bent to pick up the key.

“Leave it,” said the other man.

For the first time, their voices sounded different. His father's was younger.

The boy reached for the thread. His mother tried to lift it away, but he caught it between finger and thumb.

He could feel knots in it. Hundreds of them, close together.

“Which one is tomorrow?” he asked.

Anne knelt beside him.

“None of them yet.”

“Then we don't have to go.”

His mother made a sound he had only heard once before, through a bathroom door.

Outside, a car horn sounded twice.

His grandmother never came to their house."
